body: Ah, upon reading the summary more carefully, the issue you intended to report may be slightly different. > What I would expect to happen, is when I fire the oneshot during fadeout it would stop fading out and begin fading in against the previous oneshot. If you want to retain the previous fade-out state and then fade in on top of it, this is currently impossible with the NodeOneShot implementation. Just as the StateMachine does not currently perform two or more blends simultaneously, NodeOneShot can only process two animations at a time ("in" and "shot"). As a workaround, I believe creating multiple NodeOneShots using an approach similar to the simultaneous audio playback queue would be the workaround. _Edited:_ I found what you're saying is the problem. It does appear that the effects of the previous fade-out are unintentionally lingering.
I've sent https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115125, please check it if you can.

> I've sent [#115125](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115125), please check it if you can.

I have checked it out, but this stuff goes over my head a bit so I am struggling to understand it.
I would need to test it on my MRP to see how it changes to know for sure, but I think this might not solve the issue I am talking about in particular.

My issue is that I change the `shot` animation during fadeout time, which causes the oneshot node to blend the new `shot` animation over fadein time against the `in animation.
The only way for me to prevent this is to either chain oneshot nodes (which is not "feasible" in my solution as I already have 6 oneshots and it would be cumbersome to have 12/18).

or detect when the oneshot is currently fading out (internal_active is false, active is true indicates fading out) and if so remove all fadein time so it doesn't have any time to blend with the `in`.

However as you mentioned above, that is not possible because the oneshot cannot blend animations that do not exist, the moment I change the `shot` animation all that remains is `in` and `shot`.

I personally think, but there is likely a good reason against this, that when the `shot` changes during fadeout time, it should cache the previous `shot` pose and the rest of fadeout time should use that cached pose as the `in`.

I would love to try out https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/115125, but it isn't in any engine version yet, just committed?

Thanks for explaining that, this commit doesn't erase the issue I am having, but it does make it look far better.

In my original uploaded video the playback jitters badly when playing animations during fadeout, but in the new video it cleanly fades in using the `in` and `shot` animations.

As for my issue, is there no potential solution aside from chaining oneshots?
I know if I change the `shot` animation whilst the oneshot is running, it wont end until the **new** animation finishes. The exception being if the oneshot is fading out it will end regardless.

Can that be tweaked, or maybe have a checkbox toggle on the node itself? Make it so if the `shot` animation changes **during** fadeout, it blends back against a cached pose of the previous `shot`?

Or is this something that is not feasible to add in the engine and it is my responsibility to work around the limitation?

> Or is this something that is not feasible to add in the engine and it is my responsibility to work around the limitation?

I think it's difficult to do more than this without fundamental reworking NodeOneShot. As I commented above https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115095#issuecomment-3767837077, if we were to implement it, it would require reworking to manage the playback time position of all  animations shot up to that point using a queue array. Therefore, chaining OneShot to implement a queue on the user side is the currently available workaround.

The problem with implementing queue method to NodeOneShot internally is that it can be expected to corrupt them when chained animation node is nested (similar problem is https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/13307#issuecomment-3404347489). It might be implementable if there were a constraint limiting Shot input to NodeAnimation, but it would probably be wiser to add a separate Node distinct from NodeOneShot.
